meta.title: Competitor Radar
meta.niche: Family location sharing, driving safety, and family-safety mobile apps

analysis.summary: Bark and Qustodio publish steadily on kids' online safety. Life360 published nothing in 30 days, and GeoZilla and Google Family Link were also quiet.

points.text: Bark is the most active, with 18 new pages and 19 updates, much of it school and institution content.
Qustodio publishes parent-education articles and research (4 new, 3 updated) and does not push a product.
Find My Kids launched 4 pages on one idea: tracking elderly parents. Three are translations, so this is a small test.

Bark.play: Mixes parent guides on trending risks with case studies and landing pages for schools, foster care and Medicaid.

Qustodio.play: Explains online risks and teen wellbeing with guides and research, plus a new Alert resources page.

GeoZilla.play: No new or updated pages in 30 days. Small site of 15 pages.

Find My Kids.play: Launches one elderly-parent tracking page in English, Estonian, Lithuanian and Chinese.

Google Family Link.play: No new or updated pages in 30 days. Most of the site is international copies.

Life360.play: No new or updated pages in 30 days across 101 pages.

shared.title: Trending-risk parent guides
shared.text: Bark (TikTok, iOS 27, gaming bullying) and Qustodio (maxxing, impersonation, teen loneliness) publish quick guides on current worries. They win parents who search when a new risk appears.

shared.title: Research as authority
shared.text: Bark has 6 research pages and Qustodio has 2. Both back their advice with surveys and studies. Life360 can use its own location and driving data the same way.

gaps.title: Elderly-parent location sharing
gaps.text: Only Find My Kids covers it, and only with 4 new pages. Life360 could own the adult-family and aging-parent angle with real guides.

gaps.title: Driving safety research and teen driver guides
gaps.text: None of the active competitors publish on driving safety in this data. Life360 could lead with teen driver guides and data.

gaps.title: Fast guides on new phone and app changes
gaps.text: Bark covers iOS 27 and trends. Life360 could publish quick guides on location privacy, new OS features and family-safety setup.
